A rock gong is a slab of rock struck like a drum, an example of a rock instrument. Rock gongs have been found in Africa, Asia and Europe. Regional names for the rock gong include kungereng, kwerent dutse, gwangalan, kungereng, kongworian and kuge. Apart from 'kuge' (Hausa for a double iron bell) and 'dawal' (Ge'ez for a church rock gong), these names are onomatopoeic.
石鑼為體鳴樂器，發聲體是整塊岩石板，常見大型輝綠岩，幾乎完全實心；若非完全實心，: The rock gong is an idiophone; the sounding body is a whole slab of rock, often large dolerite, almost completely solid; if it is not quite solid the timbre is hollower and less metallic. It is played by striking the surface of the rock with a stone held in the hand, mostly igneous rock, though metamorphic quartzite has also been found. The source does not state the other parts.
石鑼的明確起源年代未見於來源，但已知標本分布於非洲、亞洲與歐洲。非洲發現地點包括: The source gives no clear date of origin for the rock gong, but specimens are known from Africa, Asia and Europe. African find sites include Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria, Sudan, Siyu and Ugauha in Tanzania, the Serengeti, Uganda and Zambia. The Kupgal rock-art site in India was found in 1892 and rediscovered in the twenty-first century; it belongs to the Neolithic and holds many rock gongs and rock paintings. In June 1955 the earliest recorded find of a rock gong was made at Birnin Kudu in Nigeria; in 1956 the archaeologist Bernard Fagg brought it to anthropological attention and noted that the distribution of rock gongs is close to the position of cave paintings.
石鑼音色清亮而富有穿透力，具有明快、堅實的質感。其音響特徵因石材密度而異，敲擊時: The rock gong has a clear, penetrating timbre, with a bright, firm quality. Its sound varies with the density of the stone; struck, it gives a crisp impact with a short resonant tail. Its range is relatively high, mostly a middle- and high-frequency metallic quality with a slight raw coarseness. Its resonance is simple and the sound dies away quickly, not sustained like a bronze instrument. Beside the bronze gong, the rock gong sounds cleaner and sharper, without the low-frequency weight; beside drums, it has a stronger sense of pitch and a more metallic quality. Its sound is plain and direct, with a strong flavour of the original peoples, and it is often used to underpin rhythm and in ritual music.
